sources.title: The Encyclopedia of Empire: Kadamba Kingdom
sources.note: Specialist encyclopedia entry used only for the overview: origins around Talagunda, Banavasi center, wider reach and absorption into the Chalukya political system.

sources.title: IGNOU: Early State Formation in the Deccan
sources.note: University history module used for Talagunda, Pallava conflict, named regions, local groups, royal charters and the Sanskritization of Deccan epigraphy.

sources.title: IGNOU: Kingdoms in the Deccan and the South
sources.note: University history unit used for founder tradition, Banavasi and Palasika branches, rival neighbors and Chalukya absorption by about 575.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: Talagunda Inscription of Santivarman
sources.note: Primary inscription edition and summary used for Mayurasarman, Kanchi study, Pallava conflict, royal genealogy, marriage diplomacy, Kubja and the Talagunda tank.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica VIII: Talagunda Pillar Inscription
sources.note: Foundational epigraphic edition used for the Sanskrit founder narrative, Kanchi episode, heroic conflict and named poet Kubja.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: Gudnapur Inscription of Ravivarman
sources.note: Primary inscription edition and summary used for Ravivarman’s genealogy, claimed victories, archery, horses, elephants and political learning.

sources.title: Cecil and Gomes: Kama at the Kadamba Court
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study used for the Gudnapur pillar as a text-monument, Kama temple inside the royal residence and agrarian support for its maintenance.

sources.title: Bisschop and Cecil: Jainism and Royal Representation in the Kadamba Plates of Palasika
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study used for fifth- and sixth-century Halsi as northern capital, four generations of plates, Jain institutions, donors and Sanskrit royal representation.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: The Halmidi Inscription
sources.note: Scholarly translation used for the oldest surviving Kannada inscription, revised date, military-service land reward, tax waiver and disputed link to the main Kadamba court.

sources.title: INFLIBNET: South Indian Kingdoms, Pallavas and Chalukyas
sources.note: University chapter used for Kirtivarman I’s 566 to 597 reign and campaigns against the Kadambas, Nalas and Mauryas.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica VI: Aihole Inscription of Pulakesin II
sources.note: Primary 634 CE Chalukya praise inscription used cautiously for its retrospective claim that Kirtivarman destroyed Kadamba power.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Indian Archaeology 1994 to 1995, A Review
sources.note: Official excavation report used for Banavasi’s Chutu, Satavahana, Kadamba and post-Kadamba sequence and the limits of a small trial trench.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Indian Archaeology 1995 to 1996, A Review
sources.note: Official follow-up excavation report used for Kadamba-period structural activity, ceramics, small finds and rain-interrupted fieldwork inside the fortified town.

sources.title: Uthara Suvrathan: Complexity on the Periphery, Banavasi
sources.note: University of Michigan dissertation used for the fifty-square-kilometer survey, Banavasi as a durable regional center, craft sites, possible ring well and severe dating disturbance.

sources.title: H. Thakur: Early Historic Material Culture at Banavasi
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological synthesis used for the fifth-century fort repair, pottery, tools, ornaments, beads, terracottas and the mostly pre-Kadamba dates of many finds.

sources.title: Govindraya Prabhu Sanoor: Coins of the Banavasi Kadambas
sources.note: Numismatic study used for Banavasi geography, uncertain ruler attributions, dated coin exceptions, split branches and the caution required by an unproven hoard context.

sources.title: George M. Moraes: The Kadamba Kula
sources.note: Older historical synthesis used cautiously for competing ruler chronologies, royal marriage traditions and the inscriptional reference to physician and official Nilakantha.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: Devagiri Plates of Mrigesavarman, Year 3
sources.note: Primary charter record used for a Jain caityalaya, named administrators, calendrical detail and land-measure vocabulary under Mrigesavarman.

sources.title: G. S. Gai: Kuntagani Plates of Ravivarman, Year 12
sources.note: Primary charter record used for measured land, a Veda-linked recipient, regnal dating and the agrarian base behind elite donations.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Excavations of a Brick Apsidal Temple at Banavasi
sources.note: Official report used to separate Banavasi’s Satavahana-period brick religious structures from later Kadamba occupation and patronage.

proposedOverrides.summary: Historical independence ended about 575; the atlas color continues to its 600 seam.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id is kadambas, displayed Kadambas and indexed circa 500 to 600 CE; the card prioritizes the early Banavasi-centered dynasty.
Initial coverage records one 500 to 600 border interval, one border file, an imported summary and no card or override.
The exact feature is absent at 300 and 400 CE, present once at 500 CE, and absent at the indexed 600 endpoint and at 700 CE.
The 500 CE target is one Polygon with one part, one ring and ten positions; bounds are [74.15174151741519,12.151407078656504,77.47097470974711,14.967508013942592].
The raw coordinate SHA-256 is 73a3f6bba41f674da21c7e72e1700158e4752cecbd566398e2540d501e82f9a4; canonical hash is 32cfb19c27d225087e4508640dd662b2b845688257c73f2b972e1964d7a590ad.
The polygon contains Banavasi, Talagunda, Sirsi and Shivamogga but excludes Halsi/Palasika, Goa, Belagavi, Dharwad, Hubballi and the coast.
At 500 the atlas assigns Palasika/Halsi to vakataka; at 600 it assigns Banavasi and Palasika to chalukyas. Both are display assignments, not primary-source borders.
Western Gangas, Pallavas, Vakataka, Vishnu-Kundins, Chalukyas, Chola, Chera and Pandya identities remain separate exact atlas records.
Every coordinate describes imported display geometry only; it does not prove ethnicity, language, migration, modern borders or exclusive ancient sovereignty.
